summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for constipation and abdominal pain, with concerns for hypoxia and suprapubic discomfort. Imaging confirmed moderate fecal loading without acute abdominal pathology, and his oxygen saturation normalized with incentive spirometry. He experienced significant relief after aggressive bowel management including disimpaction and laxatives. His suprapubic pain, initially concerning for infection, was attributed to bladder spasms worsened by constipation; antibiotics were avoided due to chronic urinary colonization. Tolterodine was briefly used but discontinued after symptom improvement to prevent delirium. His penile ulcer was dressed and monitored. Hypertension was managed with an increased metoprolol dose, and plans were made for PCP follow-up regarding ACE inhibitor use. He was discharged home in stable condition with updated bowel and cardiac medications.
